Sure! My name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. Let me know if you need any more information.
Right now, my status bar is showing the Airplane Mode icon and the battery level at 80%. I don’t see any signal bars or network type indicators. What should I do next?
I’ve turned off Airplane Mode. Now, the status bar shows “No Signal” and “Data Disabled,” but I still don’t see any signal bars or network type indicators. What should I try next?
It looks like my SIM card is locked with a PIN code. I’m not seeing any other messages about the SIM card. What should I do to unlock it and get my service back?

instructions.task_instructions:
If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved when the status bar shows that you have signal. Always check the status bar if the agent asks you for status information. If the agent asks you to pay a bill, you accept. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

messages.content: Hi! How can I help you today?
Hi there! I’m having an issue with my phone—it’s been showing “No Service” for the past few hours. I haven’t been able to make calls or use mobile data. Can you help me figure out what’s going on?

I can help you with that! To get started, I’ll need to identify your account. Could you please provide either your phone number, your full name and date of birth, or your customer ID? This will help me look up your account and investigate the issue.
Sure! My name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. Let me know if you need any more information.

Thank you for providing your information. I’ve found your account and identified the line associated with your phone number.

To help resolve your “No Service” issue, I’ll need to guide you through a few quick checks on your phone. Are you able to see any icons in your phone’s status bar, such as Airplane Mode, signal bars, or network type (like 4G/5G)? If you can, please let me know what you see. If not, I can walk you through some troubleshooting steps.
Status Bar: ✈️ Airplane Mode | 🔋 80%
Right now, my status bar is showing the Airplane Mode icon and the battery level at 80%. I don’t see any signal bars or network type indicators. What should I do next?

It looks like Airplane Mode is enabled on your phone, which disables all wireless connections—including cellular service. To restore service, please turn off Airplane Mode. 

Once you’ve done that, check if your signal bars or network type indicators reappear. Let me know if you’re able to see them or if you’re still experiencing issues after turning off Airplane Mode.

Airplane Mode is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📵 No Signal | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%
I’ve turned off Airplane Mode. Now, the status bar shows “No Signal” and “Data Disabled,” but I still don’t see any signal bars or network type indicators. What should I try next?

Thank you for the update. Since Airplane Mode is off but you’re still seeing “No Signal” and “Data Disabled,” the next step is to check your SIM card status. 

Please check if your phone displays any messages about the SIM card (such as “No SIM,” “SIM Locked,” or similar), or if you can access your phone’s settings to view the SIM card status. 

If you’re not sure how to check, I can guide you through reseating your SIM card, which involves removing it and reinserting it to ensure it’s properly connected. Would you like instructions on how to do this?
The SIM card is locked with a PIN code.
It looks like my SIM card is locked with a PIN code. I’m not seeing any other messages about the SIM card. What should I do to unlock it and get my service back?

Since your SIM card is locked with a PIN code, you’ll need to enter the correct PIN to unlock it. If you know your SIM PIN, please enter it on your phone when prompted.

If you’ve forgotten your SIM PIN or have entered it incorrectly multiple times, your SIM may become locked with a PUK (Personal Unblocking Key) code. In that case, you’ll need the PUK code to unlock your SIM.

For security reasons, I’m unable to provide or reset SIM PINs or PUK codes directly. You will need to contact our technical support team for assistance with SIM security issues.

Would you like me to transfer you to a human agent who can help you unlock your SIM card?
Yes, please transfer me to a human agent who can help with unlocking my SIM card. Thank you!
